paper.title_en: Spin-current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in $p$-wave antialtermagnets
paper.abstract_en: We show that $p$-wave magnetic insulators efficiently generate magnetization via a linear thermal magnon Edelstein effect. Furthermore, they can generate perfectly nonreciprocal spin currents through a purely even-order nonlinear response. This makes them promising candidates for spin-current rectification. More generally, we find that odd-parity-wave magnets with coplanar ground states host magnons with zero magnetic moment in the plane. Instead the magnons carry a colinear, out-of-plane magnetic moment, placing coplanar odd-parity-wave magnets within the class of antialtermagnets. We establish these general results using symmetry arguments and demonstrate them explicitly for a two-dimensional model with a coplanar ground state containing the minimal number of sublattices, inspired by the ground state of CeNiAsO. Our conclusions hold both in the absence and in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.
